parsed.title: Design Thinking & Design Principles (Electronic Commerce)
parsed.description: An 8-week course for university students on applying human-centered design thinking and core design principles to create innovative electronic commerce solutions. The course covers the entire process from ideation and business modeling to prototyping, information architecture, and visual design.

sections.title: Section 1: Introduction to Design Thinking
topics: What is Design Thinking? A Human-Centered Approach
The Core Principles: People, Technology, and Business
Understanding the Spaces of Design Thinking: Problem vs. Solution

sections.title: Section 2: The Discovery Phase: Observation and Ideation
topics: The Observing Phase: Understanding Users and Markets
Research Techniques: Qualitative and Quantitative Methods
The Ideating Phase: From Environmental Changes to Market Creation
Sources of Entrepreneurial Inspiration

sections.title: Section 3: Business Modeling and Hypothesis Testing
topics: Introduction to the Business Model Canvas
Deconstructing the 9 Building Blocks of the Business Model
Hypothesis Testing for Value Creation
Developing and Refining Hypotheses with the Test Card

sections.title: Section 4: Prototyping and Lean Methodologies
topics: The Agile Manifesto: Core Values and Principles
The Lean Startup Program: Canvas, Customer Development, and Agile
Defining the Minimum Viable Product (MVP)
The Prototyping Process: From Brainstorming to User Feedback

sections.title: Section 5: Prototyping Techniques in Practice
topics: Storyboarding: Visualizing the User Journey
Sketching: Rapid UI and User Flow Ideation
Wireframing: Creating the Blueprint of Your Product
Prototypes vs. Mockups: From Interaction to Visual Fidelity

sections.title: Section 6: Information Architecture (IA)
topics: Introduction to Information Architecture and Navigation
The 8 Principles of Effective IA
The Value of IA for Users and Businesses
Key Processes: Content Grouping, Sitemaps, and User Testing
Content Organization Models: Single Page, Flat, and Hierarchical

sections.title: Section 7: Fundamentals of Visual Design
topics: Visual Perception: Sensation, Perception, and Cognition
Applying Gestalt Principles: Similarity, Proximity, and Closure
Applying Gestalt Principles: Continuation, Figure-Ground, and Focal Point
Core Elements: Branding, Layout, and Composition
Core Elements: Color, Typography, and Motion

sections.title: Section 8: Design Implementation and Accessibility
topics: Analyzing Design Patterns in E-Commerce
The Role of Copywriting in User Experience
Introduction to Web Accessibility (WCAG)
Practical Accessibility: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust
